newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo says will continue forex policy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo says will continue forex policy.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said Wednesday the nation will continue with its current flexible exchange rate policy.

"The government considers that under current conditions the best foreign exchange rate policy to support those (economic) objectives (of the government) is precisely the flexible exchange rate," Zedillo said speaking here in northern Mexico at the close of a conference of the Mexican Institute of Financial Executives.

Zedillo said the government "will continue firmly with a flexible exchange rate policy given that is the one that will guarantee the financial equilibrium of the country with all certainty and without traumatic exchange rate movements."
He said it was the policy that will best contribute to maintaining export competitiveness, which he said must continue as the motor of economic growth in "coming years".
"To allow market forces to determine the exchange rate is the best guarantee that it will move in tandem with the necessary export development of the country that is a priority," he added.
